context: Fix the driver formulas (TPC-H and TPC-DS), make the calculator the single source of truth (driver delegates or a test asserts equality), add a magnitude regression test, and sweep exported-schema consumers for double-count assumptions. Small, surgical; blocks any throughput evidence publication.
description:
2026-07-21 adversarial UAT review finding (P1): benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py:374 computes throughput_at_size = (num_streams * 3600 * SF) / total_time, omitting the x22 queries-per-stream factor required by TPC-H spec 5.4.2.2 ((S x 22 x 3600 x SF) / Ts); the comment above documents the wrong formula as intended. The repo's own TPCMetricsCalculator.calculate_throughput_at_size (benchbox/core/results/metrics.py:64-95) implements the spec correctly and disagrees with the driver by exactly 22x. TPC-DS twin defect at benchbox/core/tpcds/benchmark/runner.py:1428 (x99).

The DRIVER value is what ships: result_capture.py:1574 -> ThroughputTestPhase -> adapter.py:893 -> schema.py:1420-1421 exports summary.tpc_metrics.throughput_at_size; QphH derived at adapter.py:896-897 is ~sqrt(22) = 4.7x low. Meanwhile benchbox metrics (cli/commands/metrics.py:178) recomputes via the correct calculator, so CLI output contradicts the exported JSON for the same run. Never caught because the only production check is throughput_at_size > 0 (tests/uat/throughput.py:259-263).

Historical exported results understate the metric; handle by documentation (CHANGELOG correction note), never by retro-editing published bundles.

anti_patterns.dont: change TPCMetricsCalculator to match the driver
anti_patterns.instead: fix the driver and keep one source of truth
anti_patterns.why: the calculator implements the spec formula; the driver is the wrong side of the 22x disagreement

anti_patterns.dont: leave the UAT-side check at throughput_at_size > 0
anti_patterns.instead: assert driver == calculator in tests and add a plausibility band in validate_throughput_result
anti_patterns.why: a 22x magnitude error sailed through it

anti_patterns.dont: retro-edit or rescale historical exported results/bundles
anti_patterns.instead: document the correction and which result versions are affected
anti_patterns.why: changelog policy forbids retrospective edits; published bundles are records

preserves.behavior: Per-query timing rows and power-phase metrics untouched.
TTT measurement window semantics (first-stream-start to last-stream-end over completed streams) unchanged.
benchbox metrics CLI output remains spec-correct (it already is).

prior_art.concept: validate_throughput_result metric check - the seam for a plausibility band

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit -k 'throughput and (metric or at_size or formula)' -q
verifications.expected: driver == TPCMetricsCalculator; synthetic S=3 SF=1 TTT=3600 yields 66.0

verifications.description: Nightly lane green with corrected metric
verifications.expected: sweep passes; exported throughput_at_size reflects the x22 correction and the assert step still validates streams

work_units.evidence: Both throughput drivers now pass actual executed-query totals to TPCMetricsCalculator; formula-focused unit selection passes 12 tests.
work_units.summary: Fix driver formulas: throughput/runner.py:374 (x22 via queries-per-stream, not hardcoded) and tpcds/benchmark/runner.py:1428 (x99); derive the factor from the actual per-stream query count

work_units.evidence: Canonical calculator parity is pinned at S=3, SF=1, TTT=3600 => 66.0; legacy TPC-DS runner also asserts parity. Formula selection passes 11 tests.
work_units.summary: Single source of truth: delegate to TPCMetricsCalculator or assert driver == calculator in a regression test (S=3, SF=1, TTT=3600 -> 66.0, not 3.0)

work_units.evidence: Consumer sweep found pass-through only in result_capture/schema and geometric mean only in adapter (no compensating multiplier). Nightly DuckDB TPCH SF1 lane passed 1/1; exported 66 queries over 815ms produced 291533.74 and UAT plausibility=ok. CHANGELOG documents non-retroactive correction.
work_units.summary: Sweep consumers (result_capture.py:1574, adapter.py:893-897, schema.py:1420) for compensating double-counts; add a plausibility band to the UAT throughput validator; CHANGELOG correction entry
